reviews.comment: His homework was super difficult and no one in the class understood anything he was doing ever. I think I did better studying on my own then going to lecture. The only thing that kept the class afloat was the fact he curved the heck out of all our tests. I had him for 211 also and he was equally as bad there.

In reality just take him. He curves the exam so the median is around a 90, so you really do get 15+ curves on the exam. Homework is straigthforward-ish, but it isn't too bad. He's certainly a professor you can't go wrong with taking!

He's a cool dude. He constantly ask if you have questions but nobody replies. Feel sorry for him on that. His handwriting is tough to read, but you will overcome it. Homework is reasonable, it's all online. Unfortunately with webassign. And he curves the midterms like crazy.

I am a freshman statistics major and already knew most of the STAT 211 material, however still went to most lectures and thought he explained the material in a way that made it easy for anyone to understand. Very knowledgeable in the statistics field and curves the test very generously. Hardest part of the class is learning R to code for homework.

So I am a freshman taking differential equations at the same time at STAT 211. STAT 211 is way harder for me. It is just really hard to learn the material. I could imagine myself doing really well if I knew statistics before. He adds 15-25 points to each test so if you know some already you could get great grades. Homework is hard, lots of R.

I certainly learnt a lot in this class. Dr. Katzfuss is very accessible to students and makes them know he cares. The class wasn't too difficult and the material was presented in a very orderly manner (well, he is German). I have no clue where the negative comments about his classes come from. His class was a great experience for me.

He uses Top hat for questions and to watch lectures beforehand. The homework is tough, go to help sessions (very helpful to solidify knowledge). I didn't really watch lectures before class because he explained it very well for me. Test were easy if you were able to understand the practice tests and he gives big curves. Help sessions make an easy A

Dr. Katzfuss is incredibly intelligent and well-versed in Statistics. However, he lacks the ability to bring his knowledge down to a level that introductory level Statistics students can understand. Homework is tough, tests are tough, and his explanations rarely bring clarity to the topic at hand. Utilize your TA and other resources.

Always lectures monotonously. Class is more theoretical; without calculus background some concepts may be hard to grasp conceptually. Probably a major gap in difficulty depending on whether or not you took AP Statistics - I did and the only extra material I really gained was snippets of R code which weren't in-depth enough.

Horrible professor. He's so boring, never does examples in class so the homework is very hard and doesn't correlate to the lectures at all. This was supposed to be a flipped classroom, so we watched the lectures online before class, then in class, he would give the same lecture again, puts you to sleep. DO NOT TAKE.

The only good thing about him is that he gives a huge curves. His curve is a reflection of how little he has taught us. The exams were only curved that much because we learned absolutely nothing in class. The homeworks are all R based and have very little to do with the actual exams.
So he's pretty solid, just kinda boring. The TA's are helpful. The tests will save your grade make sure to study well for them, they aren't hard.
